mangaian_tangaroa.name: First coconut buds
mangaian_tangaroa.notes: Gill records the first buds of newly planted coconut groves as the offering at Tangaroa’s Mangaian marae.

sources.reference: William Wyatt Gill, Myths and Songs from the South Pacific (1876), pp. 19

polynesian_kanaloa.name: Hauola at Hoea, Waiawa, Kauai
polynesian_kanaloa.notes: Beckwith records the joint worship of Kane and Kanaloa at Hauola.

sources.reference: Martha Beckwith, Hawaiian Mythology (1940), ch. V, pp. 60–66

polynesian_kane.name: Hauola at Hoea, Waiawa, Kauai
polynesian_kane.notes: Beckwith records the joint worship of Kane and Kanaloa at Hauola.

sources.reference: Martha Beckwith, Hawaiian Mythology (1940), ch. V, pp. 60–66

polynesian_tangaroa.name: Fishing karakia
polynesian_tangaroa.notes: Incantations ask Tangaroa and other gods for fish; the article records a Ngāti Porou example.

sources.reference: Paul Meredith, Te hī ika – Māori fishing (2012), Traditional practices, Religious rites, First fish and Talismans

polynesian_tangaroa.name: First fish
polynesian_tangaroa.notes: Fishers return the first catch to the sea or leave fish at shore offering places.

sources.reference: Paul Meredith, Te hī ika – Māori fishing (2012), Traditional practices, Religious rites, First fish and Talismans

polynesian_tangaroa.name: Te Naenae near Mōkau
polynesian_tangaroa.notes: The article identifies this place as a site of fish offerings to Tangaroa.

sources.reference: Paul Meredith, Te hī ika – Māori fishing (2012), Traditional practices, Religious rites, First fish and Talismans

mangaian_rupe.name: Travel in a bird’s body
mangaian_rupe.notes: Rupe enters a linnet and visits his sister Ina across the sea.

sources.reference: William Wyatt Gill, Myths and Songs from the South Pacific (1876), pp. 94–95

mangaian_ngaetua.name: Visit Ina in bird form
mangaian_ngaetua.notes: Ngaetua and Vaitooringa come to their daughter and grandchildren in the form of birds.

sources.reference: William Wyatt Gill, Myths and Songs from the South Pacific (1876), pp. 94

mangaian_vaitooringa.name: Visit Ina in bird form
mangaian_vaitooringa.notes: Vaitooringa and Ngaetua come to their daughter and grandchildren in the form of birds.

sources.reference: William Wyatt Gill, Myths and Songs from the South Pacific (1876), pp. 94

mangaian_motoro.name: Speak through Papaaunuku
mangaian_motoro.notes: Motoro’s spirit possesses his first priest and speaks oracles through him.

sources.reference: William Wyatt Gill, Myths and Songs from the South Pacific (1876), pp. 27
E. W. Gifford, Tongan Myths and Tales (1924), pp. 16

mangaian_motoro.name: Hibiscus wood
mangaian_motoro.notes: The spirit travels to Mangaia on hibiscus after the body is devoured by sharks.

sources.reference: William Wyatt Gill, Myths and Songs from the South Pacific (1876), pp. 27

tongan_laufakanaa.name: Fishing net brought from the sky

sources.reference: E. W. Gifford, Tongan Myths and Tales (1924), pp. 16–17
